transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?

Well, thanks for seeing me, Doc. I came in because... well, ever since my father-in-law moved in with us, things have just been a bit much. I’ve been holding it together at work alright, but at home and with my coursework, I’m just a lot more wound up and short-tempered than I’m used to being. 

I've also started skipping the things that usually keep my head clear. I haven't been fishing, I've ignored my woodworking projects, and I'm even skipping the first-aid workshops I usually go to. I just haven't been myself lately and figured I should probably talk to someone about it.
When exactly did your father-in-law move in with you, and did you start feeling this way around that same time, or were you already feeling wound up and short-tempered before he arrived?

He moved in about four months ago. And no, I definitely wasn't feeling like this before he got here. Things were pretty normal then. 

I'd say I really started noticing the strain within the first couple of months of him being with us. You know, just as our new home routines and all the extra caregiving demands really settled in... that's when I started getting so wound up.
If your father-in-law were to move out tomorrow, do you think these feelings of being wound up and short-tempered would go away, or do you think they would stick around?

I think they'd probably go away. I mean, there hasn't really been a stopping point yet to know for sure, because he's still living with us. We're just... we're still adjusting to the whole caregiving setup, day in and day out. But yeah, if he moved out and we had our normal routine back, I really do think I'd settle back down.

You mentioned feeling wound up and short-tempered, and that you've been skipping your usual activities. Beyond the irritability, have you been experiencing other symptoms like trouble sleeping, difficulty concentrating, or physical tension in your body?

No, not really. I mean, my sleep is fine, and I haven't noticed any real trouble focusing or, you know, any physical tension like you mentioned. It's really just the irritability and feeling so wound up, and just... not having the drive to do my usual hobbies. That's pretty much it.
Besides feeling wound up and irritable, have you been experiencing a lot of worry or nervousness about things in general, or is it more that you're just frustrated with the situation at home?

No, I wouldn't say I'm worried or nervous about things. It's... yeah, it's definitely more just frustration with the situation at home. I don't really have any general worry going on, I'm just fed up and irritated with how my day-to-day life is right now.

You mentioned your father-in-law moved in about four months ago and things got worse within the first couple of months after that. So would you say these feelings of irritability and loss of interest in your hobbies have been going on pretty much continuously for the last two to three months?

Yeah, pretty much. Actually, I'd say it's been going on for about four months now. It basically started right when my father-in-law moved into our house, and it's been pretty continuous ever since then.

When you say it's been going on for about four months, did the irritability and loss of interest in your hobbies start right away when your father-in-law first moved in, or did it take a week or two before you really started noticing these changes?

Well, let me think about that. It probably wasn't the exact day he arrived. He moved in about four months ago, but I really started noticing the strain within the first couple of months. It took a little time for our home routines to shift and for all the new caregiving demands to actually settle in. So it was more as we got into that new day-to-day reality that the irritability and everything really took hold.

So just to be clear on the timeline: your father-in-law moved in four months ago, and you started noticing the irritability and loss of interest in your hobbies sometime during those first couple of months after he arrived. Are these symptoms still going on right now, today?

Yeah, they are. There hasn't really been a stopping point yet because he's still living with us. We're still right in the middle of it, trying to figure out this whole caregiving setup, so the frustration is still very much there.

You mentioned your father-in-law moved in four months ago and you started noticing these feelings within the first couple of months after that. So roughly how many weeks or months ago would you say the irritability and loss of interest in your hobbies actually began?
I'd say it's been going on for about four months total. Like I mentioned, it all really traces back to right around the time my father-in-law moved into our house. So, yeah, roughly four months.

I want to make sure I have the timeline right. When did you first start noticing the irritability and loss of interest in your hobbies—can you give me a specific month or roughly how many weeks after your father-in-law moved in?

I guess I'm not exactly sure on a specific date or, you know, exactly how many weeks it was. Like I said, he moved in four months ago, and it just sort of built up from there. It's hard to pinpoint the exact moment it started, but it's just been a constant thing for a while now.

When you think back to the first month your father-in-law moved in, were you already feeling irritable and losing interest in your hobbies then, or did it take another month or so before those feelings really kicked in?

Well, like I was saying, he moved in about four months ago. I'd say I really started noticing the strain within those first couple of months. It wasn't instant, but as our home routines changed and the caregiving demands kind of settled in, that's when the irritability and everything else really kicked in.

During that first month after your father-in-law moved in, before the caregiving routines really settled in, were you already feeling irritable and losing interest in your hobbies then, or was that first month still pretty normal for you?

I mean, like I said, he moved in about four months ago. That first month wasn't totally normal, but the real strain... the irritability and dropping my hobbies... that really started showing up within those first couple of months. It just took a little time for the new routines and all the caregiving stuff to really settle in and start getting to me.
